transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luca (Redwood Partnerships), Alex (Titan Head of Platform), Maya (Titan VP Sales), Diego (Titan SA), Sasha (Legal), Anika (Partnerships)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Focus: co-sell motion across two priority accounts (EastGrid and HelioHealth) and readiness for Private deployment POC.
- Actionable: pipeline sharing, security checklist, benchmark run and procurement gating items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): alright hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight 45 to 60 i think we have 62 on the calendar but we'll try to be crisp. quick roll call?
[00:22] Alex (Titan): alex here, maya, diego, sasha and anika joining.
[00:30] Maya (Titan): hi all, good to see you.
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood): great, quick agenda - pipeline review for EastGrid and HelioHealth, lead ownership and co-sell crediting, security and procurement blockers for the private POC, and next steps. sound right?
[00:48] Maya (Titan): yep makes sense.
[01:05] Priya (Redwood): i'll jump into the technical bits later, specifically what scope we'd propose for the latency/cost benchmark, but first maybe jordan you want to run the commercial side?
[01:18] Jordan (Redwood): sure. so from our side we've marked EastGrid as highest velocity - you've indicated a target close in q3, approx mid august? our number there is 750k ARR if things go full term. HelioHealth is more strategic but slower - likely q4. we want to align on who owns inbound leads, and how we log partner-sourced versus partner-influenced.
[01:45] Maya (Titan): correct. EastGrid is definitely sales-engaged, i own that. helio is more of a technical evaluation - diego is lead on that.
[02:05] Diego (Titan): yes, helio will want a private deployment demo because of PHI concerns and eventual on-prem desire.
[02:22] Jordan (Redwood): that's expected. ok on co-sell crediting - our recommended approach is: partner introduces and owns the initial exec intro -> credit as partner-sourced; if we bring a deep SE-led POC after intro, mark as partner-influenced and split credit in CRM. we can provide a simple mapping sheet.
[02:50] Maya (Titan): that sheet will be helpful. question on referral discount and deal registration - does redwood offer partner registration with price protection?
[03:08] Luca (Redwood): short answer: yes, we do partner registration and basic price protection for deals that meet qualification. we'll put the exact thresholds in the playbook.
[03:22] Sasha (Titan, Legal): can you clarify what the standard T&Cs are for Dedicated/Dedicated+Private? we have to check indemnities and data residency clauses.
[03:38] Jordan (Redwood): good question - we'll attach our partner/enterprise legal pack. for Private deployments we have a slightly different addendum to handle data residency and KMS integrations. we'll flag the exact clauses for you.
[03:55] Alex (Titan): on the procurement timeline, our legal team usually needs about 3 weeks after final SOW - there's also an internal security review that looks at SOC2, SAML/SSO and KMS.
[04:15] Priya (Redwood): on the security review note, for the Private POC we can support customer-managed KMS/HSM and SAML SSO, RBAC controls, and we maintain audit logs; we'll prepare a checklist.
[04:36] Diego (Titan): perfect - that checklist will determine whether helio can move to a Private POC or needs a hosted isolated tenant first.
[04:50] Jordan (Redwood): ok moving to pipeline specifics - Maya, can you talk through EastGrid cadence? close plan? blockers?
[05:02] Maya (Titan): sure - EastGrid is finishing internal procurement, commercial terms were prelim agreed; main blocker is a short security gap from their side about key separation. they asked for an on-prem toggle but might accept VPC Private if KMS is customer-managed. timeline - they want a vendor decision by july 30.
[05:26] Jordan (Redwood): july 30 noted. that pushes closure to late july/early august at pace if procurement clears. Diego for helio what's the expected POC scope?
[05:40] Diego (Titan): helio will want 2 weeks of production-simulated traffic, latency SLOs under 200ms 95 for inference on typical clinical prompts, and evidence of encryption at rest + access controls. they'll also want a demo of model fallback for graceful degradation.
[06:03] Priya (Redwood): ok we can scope that. technical approach: we propose Redwood Dedicated with a private control plane (Private) for helio; Dedicated for EastGrid could be fine if they don't require customer-managed network. for helio the main work is network egress controls and KMS integration.
[06:25] Alex (Titan): do you have a sense of cost delta between Dedicated and Private for the POC?
[06:35] Jordan (Redwood): Private has higher onboarding and infra fees typically — usually a fixed setup + monthly platform fee; we can share a ballpark. Dedicated is more straightforward usage-based. we'll include numbers in the sheet.
[06:48] Maya (Titan): how long for a Private spin up for a POC if we get SOW signed?
[06:55] Priya (Redwood): with pre-approved templates and a partner enablement path, 2-3 weeks from signed SOW to environment ready is realistic. if there's custom networking or air-gapped on-prem work it might be longer.
[07:15] Diego (Titan): what's the benchmarking plan? i want to compare latency & token cost to their current local LLM inference.
[07:24] Priya (Redwood): we'll run two benchmark passes: (1) latency-focused under a steady state simulated load, (2) cost-focused with batching and quantization settings. we'll run with their prompt set and sequence length profile. we can produce token-level cost breakdowns and KV cache hit-rate estimates.
[07:48] Alex (Titan): do you support model variants for fallback? e.g., smaller quantized model if heavy traffic?
[07:55] Priya (Redwood): yes, smart routing and model variants are part of the platform — automatic fallback to cheaper variants with policy-based routing is supported.
[08:08] Jordan (Redwood): let's capture risk: procurement slip (2-3 week delay), security gating (legal redlines), and benchmark mismatch (if latency > 200ms). mitigation: timeline slack, pre-send legal pack, run a short smoke benchmark pre-POC.
[08:32] Maya (Titan): if procurement slips we may lose q3 target for EastGrid. we need contingency to hold seat on your side.
[08:40] Luca (Redwood): we can provide a hold with limited reservation for partner-led deals — will include options in the playbook.
[08:50] Sasha (Titan, Legal): i need to see sample SA and data processing addendum; also curious about logging and e-discovery controls.
[08:58] Jordan (Redwood): we'll share the legal pack and a short memo about audit log retention and e-discovery.
[09:12] Maya (Titan): pricing — we prefer a clear threshold for committed usage so we can model margins and incentives; are there partner-level discounts?
[09:24] Luca (Redwood): yes. partner discounts tiers are aligned to registration and joint pipeline milestones. the playbook will have a matrix.
[09:35] Diego (Titan): technical Q: in a Private deployment, does the runtime still do batching and KV cache? we need to ensure caching doesn't expose cross-tenant state.
[09:48] Priya (Redwood): good question — KV cache is tenant-isolated in Private and Dedicated; batching can be configured per-tenant and preserves KV isolation. we'll include architecture docs.
[10:05] Alex (Titan): for helio the sensitive prompts will need to avoid cloud-hosted tokens. that pushes to VPC or on-prem. what's your on-prem package like?
[10:18] Priya (Redwood): on-prem involves a longer integration window and dedicated infra shipping; we have an on-prem package for regulated customers that includes air-gapped install and customer-managed keys and local telemetry forwarding. timeline is typically 6-10 weeks depending on scope.
[10:35] Jordan (Redwood): ok circling back to next steps — i'll send the pipeline spreadsheet. Luca will put the playbook in the partner folder with registration, discounts, and legal references. Priya will scope the benchmark and we will run it with Diego's prompts.
[10:52] Maya (Titan): good. also can we schedule a deeper security deep-dive with your security lead?
[10:58] Jordan (Redwood): yes i'll request a security deep-dive; target next week if feasible.
[11:05] Sasha (Titan): i'll try to review the legal pack quickly and send redlines.
[11:12] Jordan (Redwood): excellent. any other open questions?
[11:20] Maya (Titan): curious on support model post-POC - who manages day-to-day? AE or partnership?
[11:30] Luca (Redwood): typically AE + SE during POC, then an assigned CSM + partner success manager for long-term. we'll document handoff.
[11:42] Diego (Titan): one more technical request - can redwood run a sample inference trace so we can see token-level breakdown?
[11:50] Priya (Redwood): yes, we'll provide token cost and per-call latency trace for the benchmark.
[12:02] Jordan (Redwood): great, that's the core. i'll summarize and send the sheet. would be helpful if titan can share prompts and expected QPS.
[12:15] Diego (Titan): i'll get those by the end of the week.
[12:22] Jordan (Redwood): perfect. recap: deliver legal pack, pipeline sheet, playbook folder, benchmark scope and schedule a security deep-dive.
[12:35] Maya (Titan): thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[12:42] Alex (Titan): thanks, talk soon.
[62:00] End of recording.
